citations.review_text: I'm getting the run around from Rockstar support. I can't play the game I legally own because I no longer have access to the email I registered the game with nearly a decade ago. Considering their idea of customer service is to close the ticket without helping, it's hard to recommend buying this game.

Corpo bs, glad I bought it heavily discounted and will just steal it now.

I hope Steam makes them remove these addtional utterly useless checks.

My negative review is not about the game, but about Rockstar as a provider. Account, launcher, and support issues are extremely frustrating, and Rockstar Support has been one of the worst support experiences I have had with any game publisher.

Great game, but poor customer support can completely ruin the experience.

I wish this review were about gameplay, graphics, or missions… but I haven’t been able to play any of that because I’ve been stuck dealing with Rockstar’s absurdly slow password reset system. I got locked out of my account, and what should’ve been a simple “click link, reset password, get back in” turned into a multi‑hour waiting game. For 8 Days, that’s just unacceptable.

The worst part is how outdated the whole process feels. You request a reset, and then you sit there refreshing your inbox like it’s 2005, hoping the email finally arrives. When it does, it’s often delayed so long that the link is practically useless by the time you get it. I’ve spent more time trying to regain access to the game than I’ve ever spent actually playing it on Steam.

For a studio with the resources Rockstar has, this is embarrassing. GTA 5 is supposed to be a premium experience, but the account system feels like it was built by a completely different company—one that doesn’t care about user experience at all. If you ever lose access to your account, prepare to wait, and wait, and wait some more.

I bought the game to play it, not to fight with a broken password reset system. Until Rockstar fixes this, I can’t recommend GTA 5 on Steam. A great game means nothing if you can’t even log in.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that recent updates have nerfed payouts and increased the cost of properties and items, making the economy feel like a grind.

citations.review_text:
Rockstar’s “final big score” before GTA VI is a mass economy nerf disguised as a museum heist.

And I actually bought GTA+ for this update.
Seriously? This is what I paid for?

The Kortz Center Heist should have been a celebration of GTA Online after nearly thirteen years. Instead, Rockstar used it as an excuse to make some of the game’s most popular money-making activities significantly worse, seemingly so this overpriced new heist would look generous by comparison.

To host the Kortz Center Heist at full price, a new player needs a Mansion starting at GTA$11.5 million and the mandatory Art Studio expansion costing another GTA$4.7 million.
That is GTA$16.2 million just for permission to host the content.

Even when discounted, the Art Studio is still millions for what is essentially another planning room. The Kosatka costs GTA$2.2 million and unlocks Cayo Perico. Here, Rockstar expects players to own one of the most expensive properties in the game and then purchase a separate GTA$4.7 million room inside it.

After paying that absurd entry fee, you do not receive a streamlined or uniquely ambitious heist. You get a scope-out mission, six mandatory preparation missions, five optional preparations and another finale built around driving across the same twelve-year-old map collecting equipment.
That would be acceptable if the robbery remained properly rewarding.
It does not.

Your first Primary Target sale of the week can produce a decent solo total of around GTA$2 million once secondary loot is included. Repeat the exact same content during that weekly period and the Primary Target can fall to roughly GTA$400,000.

The Mansion does not become cheaper.
The Art Studio does not become cheaper.
The preparation workload does not shrink.
The travel time does not disappear.

Rockstar simply declares that the same kind of stolen painting is suddenly worth a fraction of its previous value because you already played the new content once that week.
They describe this as “market…

I’ve played the different versions of this game for 12 years now. I’ve spent hundreds of dollars on my main account by this point
because this used to be genuinely enjoyable game. Video games are meant to be an escape from reality but GTA has seen an utterly disgusting and realistic increase in pricing on items and Rockstar Games continues to lower payouts. It’s hard to not feel betrayed after spending so much time and money on something, and for it to slowly get worse and aimed at unemployed people who have absolutely nothing better to do with their time. I just want to be able to come home from work and enjoy my game without spending hours grinding heists with ever decreasing payouts to buy stuff with ever increasing prices. At this point it is more economical to work a ten hour shift and put all the money into shark cards rather than putting those ten hours into just playing the game. GTA VI is absolutely doomed if these principles continue to the next game. Please make games for adults with lives again. Make a game that someone can just play without feeling like a chore.

I have been a longtime fan of Rockstar and this franchise. I have got this game on every console I own, and this has always been a safe go-to for me. As a fan I have stuck with it loyally, even through the wasted potential that was the abandonment of Red Dead Online. Even after having witnessed the horrendous launch of the Definitive Edition, I stuck with them because they do make good games. However, nerfing every single heist in the game to the point they are no longer profitable just to make the new update look like the most profitable heist is not just petty, but scummy. 

Rockstar claims it's to incentivize people to do other things in the game, but what they do not realize or care about is that if they actually wanted to incentivize people to try modes beyond the heists, they should actually buff the payouts of those jobs. Hype up the other game modes. Give people reason to play them. Arena War failed because it paid low and had an expensive barrier for entry. 

Their latest update reveals Rockstars true colors as a company. They are purely operating out of greed. They do not want their playerbase to stay with it. They want you to pay for shark cards and GTA+. If they find you are having fun with their games? They will find a way to make it less fun. They will punish you for enjoying their content.

These anti-consumer practices being employed by this company leaves me, as a longtime fan of this franchise and studio to say this: Do not buy this game. Do not support this company. They do not deserve your support with the way they treat their playerbase. If you need an open world crime game to play with friends, pick up Schedule 1. If open world does not matter to you as much but you still want an online crime game, pick up Payday 2. If you need a game where you and your friends just ♥♥♥♥ around doing stupid stuff, theres so many cheaper, more worthwhile indie friendslop games to choose from. But do not buy this game. Do not buy GTA+. Do not support this company…

As someone who had been playing GTAO since it came out on xbox, this update feels like a backstab. The thrill of the new heist has been completely overshadowed by the shameless changes that target grinders and solo players. Instead of improving the overall experience or finally fixing long-standing issues like the almost perennial god mode glitch, they just make solo players jump through more hoops for less payoff.
Literally no one benefits from these changes except Rockstar, who'll probably see a nice bump in Shark Card sales thanks to all the bootlickers defending these decisions.

In the end, it feels like getting a promotion that secretly comes with a hefty pay cut. **** this company.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that launching the Enhanced version automatically pops legacy achievements, removing the completionist achievement hunt.

citations.review_text:
GTA V Enhanced is still GTA V, so the game itself is great, but the achievement side was a bit disappointing for me.

The Enhanced version brings the newer PC version forward with visual and technical upgrades, and the game is still one of the best open-world titles out there. Los Santos is huge, the story is fun, the characters are memorable, and there is a massive amount of content between story mode and GTA Online.

The problem for me was the achievements. Because I already completed GTA V Legacy, launching Enhanced caused the achievements to auto-pop. On one hand, that is useful because it respects the time already spent in the older version. On the other hand, it was also a bit sad because there was no real achievement hunt left to do. For someone who enjoys working through a game and earning the 100%, it felt a little empty.

The game itself is still very easy to recommend. If you have never played GTA V before, Enhanced is probably the better version to play now. But if you already finished Legacy and care about achievements, just know that a lot of the completion experience may already be done for you.

Overall, GTA V Enhanced is still an amazing game, but the auto-popped achievements took away some of the fun for me.

claims.claim: Recent updates reduced payouts for online heists, which reviewers describe as damaging the game economy and removing incentives to play.

citations.review_text: I've loved this game ever since I first played it on my Xbox 360. I've played it on PC, PS4, and lately on PS5. The single-player is still a 10/10 experience. The online mode is fine—or at least it was before the huge nerfs to the heist final payouts. Now, I've lost all my willingness to play this game. I wanted to grind some more, but after finishing the new heist a few times, I don't even see the point anymore. You turned a great online game with a good gameplay loop into something where you only play two heists once a week and then forget about it. It's kind of sad that you see your online product as some mobile gacha cash grab. I'm looking forward to some changes, but for now, playing feels completely pointless.
I enjoyd over 1000 hours (PS4&PS5) but sadly cant recommend it anymore because online heist money nerfs..

DO NOT BUY THIS GAME. IF YOU HAVE PRE-ORDER GTA 6, CANCEL YOUR PRE-ORDER.

The update released today has officially destroyed the game. Most content, especially the most beloved content, is now no longer worth playing due to poor payouts.

This is clearly an attempt at cash grabbing by trying to make an incentive to buy in-game microtransactions, or by making you subscribe to their "GTA+" subscription. Do not buy either of those, and do not buy this game.

If you buy this game, you might as well go play a game where everything is locked behind a paywall.
Nerfed all the GTA Online heists and activities removing any incentive to play the game at all.
13 years of nickel and diming just to give every player one last kick in the balls with the heist nerfs. Story mode's okay though.

citations.review_text:
the enhanced version looks better yes,
but the Online Bugs are still there , you still get spam called by every bajeezus and their mothers and extended family , theyve removed text chat , now to text someone you need to use the phone with around 5 minutes of cooldown between messages ,from my experience and it runs like .... well ♥♥♥♥

Whoever says EA is a bad company clearly hasn't experienced a Rockstar game before. Ranging from customer support that doesn't give a modicum of a crap about the issues players experience (for example, I filled out a ticket for an issue I was having back in June, got a reply almost exactly a month later, and the agent who responded to it closed the ticket pretty much right after he messaged me, not even giving me a chance to respond), to not patching issues that have been in the game for literally years, to trying to bottleneck players into spending obscene amounts of money on microtransactions (with the alternative being tons of grinding, not helped by them nerfing the few moneymaking techniques that are actually FUN), and harshly punishing players for things that either aren't their fault - such as an ex-friend of mine being banned and having his character deleted as a consequence of something a hacker in his online lobby did - or are poorly designed/described by Rockstar themselves.

Given how much of a grind-heavy, poorly-managed experience GTA Online is (as well as how the story mode of GTA V is a considerable letdown compared to GTA IV and its DLC), I don't pity anyone who's foolish enough to buy or especially preorder GTA VI, let alone anyone who would play this one. The nicest things I can say about GTA V/Online are that the gameplay itself and graphics are pretty good, but the issues I mentioned before render this beyond salvaging.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that recent updates heavily nerf payouts for older heists, introducing diminishing returns if repeated within a week.

citations.review_text:
I just played the new heist and we were very confused on not being able to set cuts. we complete the heist, turns out the host got 2 mil. while me and a another player only got ~400k ONLY! not only does this heist not pay out well with a group, you nerf casino, cayo, dre, and knoway out buy ~30%-40%. plus ive heard you can only do a certain number of the new heist per week. 
WORST update in history.

GTA 5 is one of the best single-player games, as almost everyone knows. Right now I'm not evaluating its story mode. This review is solely about its online mode. 
Personally, I love grind games, especially achievements that are hard to obtain.  In total, I've probably put in 1,200 hours (600 hours on Steam Legacy, 100 hours on Enhanced, and about 500 hours on Xbox). Despite this, GTA Online is one of the worst games that doesn't care about your free time. The game mechanics are filled with senselessly drawn-out actions: want to take down a picture? 10 seconds of doing nothing on a screen; want to hack something? 15 seconds of waiting for a line to fill on the screen. There are countless examples like this that just drag out time, when they could have either simply cut the wait time or had an action happen in 1-2 seconds. 
The ridiculously inflated inflation is another issue. Over the years, the price of simple items has increased so much that you need to grind for several hours just to afford them. There's no need to talk about the prices of sports cars and businesses. We all know why everything is so expensive. Rockstar is an extremely greedy company; they want to sell as many Shark Cards as possible. 
The last update is so terrible, it made me decide to delete the game. I can't remember an update this bad in any game. Did I mention Rockstar is a cheap bastard? They ruined the old content, nerfed the money-making methods, I've lost count of how many times they've crippled Cayo Perico. Why? So they can milk players before GTA 6 is out. On top of that, the new content isn't good either. The Kortz Center Heist is a copy-paste of the casino heist; the setup missions are identical. You'd think it was made by AI.
Modern GTA Online has become like a mobile game, crammed with microtransactions, pay-to-win and pointlessly dragged activities. Based on Rockstar's recent actions, I'm already scared of what GTA 6 will be like in future.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the single-player campaign features an enjoyable story and entertaining protagonists, while noting weak hand-to-hand combat and sparse side content.

citations.review_text:
After finally finishing GTA V, I had a really good time with it.
The story is enjoyable, and the three protagonists are easily the strongest part of the game. Their different personalities and the way they constantly clash with each other make the story entertaining.
Driving feels great and is one of the things I enjoyed the most. On the other hand, the hand-to-hand combat feels pretty weak and outdated.
The story also has a few moments that felt a bit strange to me, especially Michael and Trevor’s first reunion. It didn’t feel as natural as I expected.
My biggest disappointment was the side content. There are some fun activities, but I honestly expected a lot more to do outside the main story.
Overall, it’s a fun game with memorable characters and an enjoyable campaign, even if it has a few weaknesses.

Even years after its release, GTA 5 remains one of the best open world games ever made. The single player story with Michael, Franklin, and Trevor is fantastic, hilarious, and well written. Los Santos feels alive and the driving and shooting mechanics still hold up beautifully. While GTA Online can be a bit of a grind if you don't want to spend real money, playing heist missions with friends is some of the most fun you can have in gaming. Absolutely worth it.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the online mode features slow, drawn-out actions and mechanics that artificially extend playtime.

citations.review_text:
GTA 5 is one of the best single-player games, as almost everyone knows. Right now I'm not evaluating its story mode. This review is solely about its online mode. 
Personally, I love grind games, especially achievements that are hard to obtain.  In total, I've probably put in 1,200 hours (600 hours on Steam Legacy, 100 hours on Enhanced, and about 500 hours on Xbox). Despite this, GTA Online is one of the worst games that doesn't care about your free time. The game mechanics are filled with senselessly drawn-out actions: want to take down a picture? 10 seconds of doing nothing on a screen; want to hack something? 15 seconds of waiting for a line to fill on the screen. There are countless examples like this that just drag out time, when they could have either simply cut the wait time or had an action happen in 1-2 seconds. 
The ridiculously inflated inflation is another issue. Over the years, the price of simple items has increased so much that you need to grind for several hours just to afford them. There's no need to talk about the prices of sports cars and businesses. We all know why everything is so expensive. Rockstar is an extremely greedy company; they want to sell as many Shark Cards as possible. 
The last update is so terrible, it made me decide to delete the game. I can't remember an update this bad in any game. Did I mention Rockstar is a cheap bastard? They ruined the old content, nerfed the money-making methods, I've lost count of how many times they've crippled Cayo Perico. Why? So they can milk players before GTA 6 is out. On top of that, the new content isn't good either. The Kortz Center Heist is a copy-paste of the casino heist; the setup missions are identical. You'd think it was made by AI.
Modern GTA Online has become like a mobile game, crammed with microtransactions, pay-to-win and pointlessly dragged activities. Based on Rockstar's recent actions, I'm already scared of what GTA 6 will be like in future.

Mainline story campaign is the only thing worth playing. Online mode is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ grind fest exclusively designed to waste your time and keep you playing, being bored and or frustrated with all the bugs/design flaws in the Online mode. GTA6 is is going to be such a chopped game the player-base will be stunned at it's release state, but it doesn't matter because a bunch of idiots will buy it anyways, the people of this world are a massive dissapointment and encourage the enshittification of everything because they don't have the self-respect to expect better quality products. they're just braindead consumers.

citations.review_text: Can`t recommend any rockstar game cause rockstar launcher. I have newer seen so bad customer support than they have in rockstar. you could imagine it would at least be decent for such of big company

Rockstar Games has become one of the most anti-consumer companies in the industry. The pricing of in-game items encourages players to buy Shark Cards or GTA+, making the grind so time-consuming that spending money becomes the practical alternative for many players.

That isn't even mentioning the numerous controversies over the years, including taking down community mods, releasing half-baked remasters, and creating unnecessary platform disparities. Rockstar, we don't want your terrible launcher or awful customer support—we want you to listen to your community.

The newest update is a perfect example of why so many players are frustrated. Older heists, which were some of the best ways to earn money, were heavily nerfed so the newest heist could become the "highest-paying" activity. The Kortz Center Heist is overpriced, underwhelming, and uninspired. Yet it seems like Rockstar expects players to rush into buying it and spend countless hours grinding through recycled content.

To anyone reading this review, I strongly recommend waiting until after GTA VI releases to see what players have to say before deciding whether it's worth your money.

#PlayersNotProfit

claims.claim: Public lobbies suffer from aggressive griefing via vehicles like the Oppressor Mk II and disruptive player behaviors such as immediate session leaving or job-warping when attacked.

citations.review_text: COMPLETELY UNBALANCED ONLINE VEHICLES LOCK ON ABUSING KIDS. OPPRESSOR ABUSING KIDS LIKE FIX THE GAME

I actually love the core of this game, but I’m leaving a negative review because if the player base doesn't push back on the current state of PC lobbies, the developers are never going to change how they handle networking and PvP.

The PvE: S-Tier
When you are actually allowed to play the game, the PvE is brilliant. The heist setups, the solo business grinding, the properties—it’s genuinely some of the best sandbox progression in gaming. If you can get into an Invite-Only lobby and just run your empire, it is an incredible experience.

The PvP & Technical State: F-Tier
Public lobbies are an absolute unplayable joke right now.

1. The Oppressor Mk II: It completely removes any actual skill or driving from vehicle combat.

2. Limp, Passive-Aggressive Tactics: People will randomly kill you when you spawn on the beach, then instantly job-warp across the map, hide inside an apartment, or leave the session the second you try to fight back. It is incredibly cowardly behavior.

3. Garbage Matchmaking: The peer-to-peer network is so outdated that the game constantly fails its connection handshakes. You will finish a mission and get consistently dumped into a public lobby completely by yourself because the game’s networking simply breaks.

4. Mod Menus & Crashes: Rockstar finally added BattlEye, but it’s completely failing against the current wave of menus. Script kiddies aren't just using menus to script-kick everyone from the session—they can literally force-crash your desktop client, forcing you to Alt+F4 and completely restart your game.

The Future (GTA 6)
With GTA 6 around the corner, Rockstar’s current direction isn’t inspiring confidence. They’ve already confirmed the sequel will be console-only at launch, physical copies are essentially digital-only (just a download code in a plastic box), it's a single-player only experience right now, and they are already locking in-game content behind a $100 Ultimate Edition paywall.

Buy this game for the solo …

claims.claim: Certain players encounter persistent technical problems such as system crashes or graphical flickering related to cloud settings.

citations.review_text: This god awful cloud or sky flickering that never seems to get fixed no matter what settings im using is diabolical. 5070ti ryzen 9 7900x3d 32 gb ddr5 man im over it.

I cannot recommend this game if you have an amd gpu as it has crashed a lot on my system (on some days every 15min) and when it crashes it always takes down the display I use for. Rendering my pc useless until I reboot the pc. However I had an crash earlier that has royally ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up my pc. It either broke my boot ssd or corrupted windows and the display driver, causing my system to be able to boot, but not being able to do anyting. 

Rockstar has always treated pc as a afterthought but an bug like this is unacceptable. This game already broke my old ps4 10 years ago and now it has broken my pc. I love this game, but I cannot support it when the developers seem to be only interested in how much money they can make from something rather then making a quality (and working) product.
Too long, didn't read: If you have an amd gpu, stay FAR away from this pile of thrash.
